s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital facial asymmetry with abnormal lip movement
salient_findings: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
key_facts: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
Normal magnetic resonance imaging of temporal bones and internal auditory canals

raw.syndrome_frame: Congenital facial asymmetry with abnormal lip movement
salient_findings: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
key_facts: Right lower lip deviates inward when smiling or crying
Normal magnetic resonance imaging of temporal bones and internal auditory canals

shortlist.label: Congenital Lower Lip Palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the specific symptom of right lower lip deviation

shortlist.label: Moebius Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Considered due to abnormal lip movement, although other symptoms are not fully matched

shortlist.label: Hemifacial Microsomia
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of congenital facial asymmetry

shortlist.label: Congenital Facial Diplegia
shortlist.why_kept: Could explain the abnormal lip movement and facial asymmetry

shortlist.label: Facial Hemiatrophy
shortlist.why_kept: A possible cause of facial asymmetry, although typically presents with more pronounced features

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of right lower lip deviation inward when smiling or crying, with symmetric facial movement at rest and normal developmental milestones, are consistent with Congenital Lower Lip Palsy.

rejected.label: Moebius Syndrome
rejected.why: Moebius Syndrome typically involves bilateral facial weakness and is often associated with other cranial nerve palsies, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Hemifacial Microsomia
rejected.why: Hemifacial Microsomia is characterized by underdevelopment of one side of the face, which is not described in this patient.

rejected.label: Congenital Facial Diplegia
rejected.why: Congenital Facial Diplegia involves bilateral facial weakness, which is not consistent with this patient's symmetric facial movement at rest.

rejected.label: Facial Hemiatrophy
rejected.why: Facial Hemiatrophy is characterized by atrophy of one side of the face, which is not described in this patient.
